game: PIT@CHI Week 12 2025, kickoff 2025-11-23 13:00 ET, CHI -3, total 46.5, outdoors

script.base: Market has Chicago leading a competitive outdoor game, not a blowout: implied CHI 24.8 / PIT 21.8 from the -3 and 46.5 close. Chicago leans on the Monangai/Swift committee and still has to throw to get to ~25; Pittsburgh stays in it, so Jaylen Warren (40 carries, 163 yards in weeks 9-11) keeps a real carry share and Chicago does not run the clock from the first quarter.
script.flip1: Chicago scores early, Pittsburgh trails and abandons the run. Warren's carries die (the 31-yard game in his last four is the template) and PIT checkdowns (Gainwell 16 targets, -9 air yards in L3) and Metcalf/Austin targets rise.
script.flip2: Outdoor weather or a defensive slog (forecast not saved) drags the 46.5 down. Both passing trees stall; the run games, especially Warren into CHI's 5.24 YPC defense, become the volume.

injury_fallout: Pre-game nflverse report, morning of kickoff, inactives not yet locked. CHI LB Tremaine Edmunds (groin), T.J. Edwards (hand) and Noah Sewell (elbow) are Out, so Pittsburgh's short/middle and run-fit group faces backups: Gainwell (16 tgt/120 yds L3), Freiermuth (8/79, not in the prop menu) and Warren benefit; Metcalf does not automatically, because he is the outside vertical (213 air yards, only 90 receiving yards L3). CHI RB Travis Homer and Roschon Johnson are Out, but they already do not appear in weeks 9-11 rush lines (Monangai 45/227, Swift 34/170, Williams 15/144, Brown 5/37), so this is not a fresh carry spike. CHI CB Jaylon Johnson (groin), CB Kyler Gordon (calf) and S Jaquan Brisker (shoulder) are Questionable: if they sit, Metcalf/Austin/Odunze matchups improve and any PIT WR under is dead; if they play, Metcalf's 6/35/49 yard slump vs a 49.5 line stays live. PIT LB Alex Highsmith is Doubtful (pectoral), so Chicago's pass game faces a thinner rush; PIT already blitzes 35% and Chicago's EPA/db is 0.24 vs blitz against 0.08 vs none. PIT QB Aaron Rodgers is Questionable (wrist): a late scratch rewrites every PIT pass leg and is unresolved. PIT DT Cameron Heyward Questionable (rest) would further soften a run defense that allows 4.33 YPC; PIT CB Darius Slay Questionable (concussion) is an outside variable for Moore/Odunze, not for Loveland.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack; shell unknown. Location splits are the stand-in: CHI allows 9.43 YPA middle (70 att), 7.53 left, 7.29 right. PIT allows 8.37 middle (123 att), 7.61 right, 5.73 left.
matchup.pressure: CHI blitzes 31%; Pittsburgh EPA/db is 0.05 vs blitz and 0.04 vs none, so Chicago pressure is not a special PIT kill or a checkdown boost. PIT blitzes 35% and Chicago feasts when blitzed (0.24 vs 0.08). Highsmith Doubtful lowers the chance that pressure actually arrives, which still helps CHI completions.
matchup.bleeds: CHI run defense is the bleed: 5.24 YPC and 38 runs of 10+ over 10 games. PIT bleeds the middle and explosives (31 passes of 20+ for 428 yards), not the run (4.33 YPC, 29 runs of 10+).
matchup.overlap: Warren's carry role (40 of PIT's RB carries in L3) runs straight into the 5.24 YPC defense and a wiped-out LB trio. Loveland (15 tgt, 213 yds, 141 air in L3) is the CHI receiving weapon aimed at PIT's middle 8.37 YPA. Odunze has the explosive profile (19 tgt, 322 air) but only 127 yards and a 0 in the last three, so the air-yard overlap is not a clean yards edge. Metcalf's 213 air yards have produced 90 yards; that is inefficiency, not overlap, and it is conditional on the CHI secondary questionables.

form: Last-four lists reconcile to the week 9-11 totals when read oldest to newest. Warren rush last three: 31, 70, 62 (2 of 3 over 52.5; L3 54.3 ypg vs a 52.5 number). His rush+rec last three (29, 91, 67) sit under 73.5 twice, and rec yards (-2, 21, 5) are all under 21.5. Loveland rec last four: 38, 118, 55, 40, every game over 31.5, L3 sum 213. Monangai's 176 is a single-game spike; the other two recent rush games are 28 and 23 against a 23.5 line, so the 75.7 L3 average is fluky. Swift L3 is 34/170 (56.7 ypg) under a 63.5 line, but his last-four rush list (124, 45, 80, 90) does not subset to 170, so that leg is unresolved. Moore's last two (0, 18) are under 42.5 after a 72; Odunze's last three (0, 86, 41) are 1 of 3 over 51.5 despite 322 air yards. Gainwell rec is 35, 4, 81 vs 12.5: volume is real, one dud is real. Metcalf last three 6, 35, 49 all under 49.5.

pre_mortem: Monday both lost because Chicago led 17-3 at half, Ben Johnson's committee (Swift 34 carries and Monangai 45 in the recent three weeks, plus Williams' 144 rush yards) ran the clock, and Loveland saw a handful of targets after Pittsburgh sat in a middle-closed look the pack never charted, finishing in the low 20s under 31.5 while the 118-yard game was the outlier the median stand-in was already fading. Warren got the early carries, then Pittsburgh trailed and the 31-yard script returned: eight carries, Gainwell in pass protection, and 52.5 never threatened. Rodgers' wrist either limited the whole offense or the final inactives, which this morning's report does not lock, flipped the plan. The counter is real on Warren (thin margin, one recent miss) and only partial on Loveland (four straight clears, but no price and no shell chart).
slip_story: One competitive-game story, not a shootout and not a favorite-clock stack: Chicago has to throw into Pittsburgh's soft middle (Loveland recyds over) while Pittsburgh can run into the worst run defense on the slate and a backup LB group (Warren rushyds over). Those two win together if the -3 holds as a one-score game. Do not add Metcalf/Odunze overs (need a pass-volume flip) or a game under (unsaved weather, and it fights Loveland). No TD legs, no second market on either player. Candidates only; bankroll script cannot price a stake with no-vig missing.
